declaration_name: Northern NSW Bushfires: 11 February 2019 onwards
official_name_if_found: Northern NSW Bushfires (11 February 2019 onwards)
main_fires: Tingha Plateau; Wallangarra; Bruxner Highway (Tabulam); Catarrh Creek Rd, Torrington; Ten Mile Rd, Deepwater; Silent Grove Rd, Torrington
summary: Dry lightning sparked several major fires across the Northern Tablelands and border region in February 2019, most seriously the Tingha Plateau fire near Inverell and the Bruxner Highway (Tabulam) fire near Kyogle/Tenterfield, both starting 10-12 Feb during an extreme-heat, high-wind outbreak. Combined, the two fires burned over 31,000 ha and destroyed at least 32 homes and 90+ outbuildings, with no lives lost. A smaller Wallangarra fire near the Queensland border also burned but caused less structural damage.

declaration_name: Bega Valley and Eurobodalla bushfires: 15 August 2018 onwards
official_name_if_found: Bega Valley and Eurobodalla bushfires (15 August 2018 onwards)
main_fires: Yankees Gap Rd, Bemboka; Wheel Gully; Potato Point Rd, Bodalla; New Buildings; Bendethera; Letts Mt Pericoe
summary: The Yankees Gap fire near Bemboka in the Bega Valley began as a private landholder's hazard-reduction burn that RFS crews left before it broke containment on 15 August 2018, in an unusually early and severe start to the 2018-19 fire season. It burned for nearly three months through about 20,000 ha of South East Forest and Wadbilliga National Parks, destroying four homes and causing an estimated $9.3 million in damage. A 2023-24 coronial inquiry examined whether the RFS should have kept crews on site longer before the burn escaped.

declaration_name: Glen Innes Severn (Highland Creek) Bushfire: 25 December 2018 onwards
main_fires: Highland Creek; Mt Sugarloaf; Ten Mile Rd, Deepwater; Barool Creek Fire; Black Mountain; Torrington Complex
summary: The Highland Creek fire broke out in the Glen Innes Severn LGA on 25 December 2018 (about 150 ha at first report), the start of a cluster of fires in the area that continued to grow through early 2019 (Mt Sugarloaf, Torrington Complex, Black Mountain), part of the same drought-driven fire season covered elsewhere by the Tenterfield/Torrington declarations (AGRN 843, 864). This should not be confused with the much larger and fatal November 2019 Glen Innes fires (Kangawalla/Diehard fire, Black Summer season) which are a separate, later event.
